office_does: The District 1 councilmember is one of seven Pierce County Council members who adopt the county budget, ordinances, taxes and land-use rules for southeast Pierce County, including Bonney Lake, Buckley, Orting, Graham and South Hill.
race_blurb: An open seat between Republican Jerome O'Leary, a commercial real-estate broker and Planning Commission chair who led the primary with 53.5%, and Democrat Kelsey Barrans, a college student-services director who chaired the Charter Review Commission and took 21.0%. They differ most on taxes, housing and transit for rural towns.

candidates.summary: Commercial real-estate broker and Pierce County Planning Commission chair running on business-minded, nonpartisan stewardship of taxpayer money.
highlights: More than 30 years in commercial real estate, earlier in commercial construction; Master Builders board member [S4]
Planning Commission appointee (confirmed 2025) and 2026 Charter Review commissioner [S2][S3]
Promises transparent decisions and responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars [S4]
Endorsed by the county Republican Party, deputy sheriffs' guild, Master Builders, realtors and Farm Bureau PAC [S5]

spending.basis: Says government should serve people 'not the bureaucracy' and pledges efficient, accountable government and stewardship of taxpayer dollars, without specific cuts.

housing.basis: Development-industry background and board role, with endorsements from the Master Builders, realtors and the Pierce County Affordable Housing Council; no stated housing mechanism.

experience.basis: Has not held elected office beyond the Charter Review Commission and says he is 'not running to be a career politician,' though he cites many county advisory boards.

candidates.summary: Green River College student-services director and Charter Review Commission chair running on infrastructure money for unincorporated areas, rural transit and housing.
highlights: Chaired the 21-member Pierce County Charter Review Commission [S3][S5]
Supports progressive taxes and higher developer impact fees [S4]
Would bring bus service to Orting, Buckley and Graham and add road capacity on rural connectors [S4][S6]
Backs public or subsidized housing investment alongside density and accessory-unit incentives [S4][S6]
Endorsed by Pierce County Democrats, the Central Labor Council, WEA and the Environmental Coalition of Pierce County [S7]

taxes.basis: Answered yes to progressive taxes as wealth increases and to raising developer impact fees in a Democratic endorsement questionnaire.

spending.basis: Wants more infrastructure funding for unincorporated areas, new rural bus service, and more funding for rural outreach and unhoused students.

housing.basis: Supports robust investment in public or subsidized housing and rent subsidies, alongside density and incentives for additional units.

safety.basis: Frames safety around structural oversight of the sheriff and proposes rural mobile outreach for homelessness; no stated position on enforcement or staffing.

climate.basis: Supports local investments to address climate change and lists community-partnered climate action among her values.

experience.basis: First council run; her only office is the Charter Review Commission, and she argues for more new candidates bringing new perspectives.
